| Question | Answer |

| a. Q3 segment with the highest net sales | consumer, 338,018,166원 |

**A judgment call you should check (a):** 48 emails are shared by more than one customer account, and for 30 of them the accounts have different segments. Your rules don't say which segment such a person belongs to. I counted each order under the segment of the account that placed it. "consumer" comes out on top whichever way it's done, but the amount changes:

| How a shared-email person's segment is chosen | consumer net sales |
|---|---|
| Segment of the account that placed the order (used) | 338,018,166원 |
| Segment of their earliest-joined account | 322,007,403원 |
| Segment of their latest-joined account | 328,972,383원 |

**Data checks:** status has three values (paid, cancelled, pending), and segments are written in six different ways that collapse to three once trimmed and lowercased. There were no refunds without a matching order line, no refunds larger than the quantity bought, and no missing values. All timestamps are in the same format. The data runs from 2025-05 to 2025-10, so October is only partly covered.
